**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** People in your community face a lot of health challenges because of the way they lead their lives and manage their environment. You are a health practitioner and you feel greatly concerned about the distressing situation. Using between 200 and 250 words, advise the people on what they must do in order to lead a healthy lifestyle. (20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Opening: who speaks and why (a health practitioner, concerned).
2. Advice in order: environment, water and hygiene, food and habits, exercise and rest, early treatment.
3. A short, motivating closing appeal.

**Model answer (229 words)**

My dear neighbours, I speak to you as your health worker, and I speak with concern. Every week, our clinic receives patients suffering from malaria, typhoid, cholera, high blood pressure and diabetes. Most of these illnesses could be prevented, because they come from the way we live and treat our surroundings.

First, keep your environment clean. Clear the bushes around your houses, cover your wells, drain stagnant water, and burn or bury rubbish instead of throwing it into gutters. Mosquitoes breed in dirty water, so sleep under treated nets.

Second, drink safe water. Boil or filter it, and wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Third, eat wisely. Choose vegetables, fruit, beans and fish more often than oil, sugar and salt. Do not overeat, and avoid too much alcohol and tobacco, which destroy the liver and the lungs.

Fourth, exercise regularly. A daily walk or farm work keeps the heart strong. Rest well, and do not hesitate to talk to a friend or a counsellor when you are troubled.

Finally, do not wait until you are seriously ill. Visit the clinic for check-ups, vaccinate your children and finish every course of treatment you receive.

Health is our greatest wealth. If each of us takes these simple steps, we shall live longer, spend less on medicine and build a stronger community. Let us start today.

**Why it earns the marks**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Content | The speaker's role is clear; the advice is specific and linked to the 'way we lead our lives and manage our environment' |
| Organisation | An opening, advice grouped in separate paragraphs, a closing appeal; 200 to 250 words |
| Style | A persuasive, direct tone (imperatives, 'we', a clear call to action), suitable for addressing a community |
| Accuracy | Correct grammar, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Under 200 or over 250 words.
2. Describing the problems at length instead of advising the people.
3. A list of slogans with no explanation, or an impolite tone that blames the audience.
